title: Second pass on the 99 'disputed choice of method' flags: adjudication
readers: Reader A: Claude (Anthropic). Reader B: Gemini 3.8 Flash (Google), blind to reader A's grades. Disagreements settled by SaneCite from the cited pages, under the rules below.
protocol: Rules R2-R6 of our 29 Oct 2026 adjudication rules
grade_labels: The page shows DEFENSIBLE, NOT DISCLOSED split by the disclosed field: 'defensible, stated in the paper' (disclosed yes) and 'defensible, not stated' (disclosed no).
rules_applied: STANDARD when the paper states the choice (text, appendix, footnote, table or figure note, or code or workbook comments) and a work the paper or the flag cites uses the same choice; showing the alternative is not required (as both readers applied it at ranks 4, 10, 46, 66, 100).
Amendment 2: the authors' own earlier papers count as cited work when the paper or the flag cites them; standard_rests_only_on_own_work records when they are the only such work.
A choice stated only by citing another paper is not counted as stated (ranks 8, 23, 102, 146).
A choice that is stated and tested for sensitivity but used in no cited work stays DEFENSIBLE, NOT DISCLOSED, with disclosed = yes (the amendment 2 gap).
Where the decisive text (a book or chapter) could not be reached and the grade turns on it, CANNOT TELL (ranks 21, 42, 85, 116, 135, 144).
RECLASSIFY yes only where the red team upheld it and the adjudicator agrees after re-running its script.
No research beyond files and pages the readers or the red team cited (R6).

rows.disclosed_basis: JEP 2014 pp.127-129 (PDF pp.7-9): data choice stated, with the caution that the data show 'mainly the location of the holding companies'
rows.note: Readers agree; kept. Reader A: The paper states its data choice and warns what it measures, but it does not show the haven share or the 20% figure on an own-income basis, and no cited comparable work using first-tier BoP income for this purpose could be shown. The alternative is disputed in the literature the flag cites (Blouin-Robinson vs Clausing), so no reclassification.

rows.disclosed_basis: JEP p.14 (PDF p.12) states the 50/50 retained-earnings rule. The underreported-income rule is not stated in the JEP (no hit for 'underreport' in the text); it is in Piketty, Saez and Zucman (2018) and its updates.
rows.note: Readers agree; kept. Under amendment 2 the authors' PSZ (2018) counts, but the underreporting rule is not stated in the JEP (PDF p.12 states only the 50/50 rule), so it cannot be STANDARD.

rows.note: Kept A. The stricter haven-year specification was run but no numbers are shown (JohannesenZucman2014.pdf PDF p.21, journal p.85: 'results not reported'). B's precedent, Huizinga and Nicodeme (2004), is cited only for its finding on information exchange (PDF p.2), not for this specification, so no cited work is shown using it.

The lower 10.3% level rests on Geerolf's 2026 gift correction, which is a dispute among researchers, not a departure from the chapter's own rule, so no reclassification.
